title: The Deposit
location: Manchester, Rusholme. Above a phone-repair shop. March.
architect_intro: A landlord. A carpet. A clock on the wall, four minutes slow. You have seen that clock before.
player_goal: Your £950 deposit back before you move to London.
stated_objection: Carpet is ruined. £350 today, cash. Tomorrow, nothing.

hidden_objection_layers.text: He never registered the deposit with a protection scheme. If the scheme is mentioned, he faces a penalty.

objects.label: Filing cabinet, bottom drawer
objects.reveals_text: Jammed half open. Where a deposit certificate would live. It's empty.

objects.label: Your move-in photos (phone)
objects.reveals_text: Dated 2 September. The carpet stain is already there, by the window.

objects.label: Wall clock
objects.reveals_text: Four minutes slow. A sticker on the back: 'Sethi & Co. Cricket Club, 1991'. Somebody's old raffle prize.

n1.speaker: nabil_haddad
n1.line: Look. Look at me. I am not a bad man. I am a man with a carpet. I take six hundred for carpet, paint, you take three-fifty, today, cash, finish. Tomorrow I'm in Beirut, you're in London, everybody is sad.

tells.reading: A clock with no reason attached to the offer.
tells.false_positive: He really is flying Friday. Check the tickets on the desk.

choices.text: That stain was there when I moved in. I have photos.

rebuttal.text: Photos, photos. Phone photos, anybody can change the date.

choices.text: Which scheme is the deposit registered with?
The offer doesn't need to expire because you're travelling. I'm not deciding against a clock.
Pay me £1,200 or I report you to the council and put your name on every review site in Manchester.

n2.speaker: nabil_haddad
n2.line: [He drums the receipts.] Carpet. Paint. Light fitting. You know what carpet costs now? My oven at home, English oven, two hundred is nothing. Everything costs.

tells.reading: He lists everything except the one word a landlord should say: scheme.
tells.false_positive: He's just upset about the carpet.

choices.text: Which scheme is it registered with, Nabil?

line_by_state.line: [Long pause. He looks at the drawer that sticks.] Scheme. Yes. The scheme. [He says nothing else for a while.] Yalla, Billo. [Quiet.] It's not... it was busy that year. My brother does the paperwork. He doesn't know I do cash.
Scheme, schedule, everything is a scheme with you students. Carpet is carpet.

choices.text: [put the dated photos on the desk] I don't want trouble for you. I'm happy to use the scheme's free dispute service, or we settle fairly today. The light fitting was broken. I'll pay for that.
So you broke the law. That's three times the deposit in penalties. Pay me double or I tell Karim.
I'll ask once more, then I'll check the scheme websites myself.
Six hundred, then. Let's split it.

n4.speaker: nabil_haddad
n4.line: [He counts out notes. Stops. Counts again.] Nine hundred. Fifty for the light, fair is fair. [He pushes it across.] You know what. My cousin has a van in Wembley. Tell him Billo sent you, he'll do London for cheap.

choices.text: Thank you, Nabil. Good luck in Beirut.

n5.speaker: nabil_haddad
n5.line: [He gets his phone out, shows you a photo of a burnt loaf.] Ka'ak. With my daughters, Sundays. Burnt. Every time. [The phone rings. He answers in Arabic, soft.] Habibti, Baba's in a meeting. [He laughs, hangs up, and for a second has forgotten you're there.]

choices.text: Get an oven thermometer. Now, about the scheme.

n6.speaker: nabil_haddad
n6.line: [Grey. He opens the till drawer and counts all of it.] Nine-fifty. Take. [He doesn't look at you.] Go to London. Good. Go.

tells.reading: He paid. He'll tell everyone why.

end_clean.architect: Nine hundred. A van in Wembley. Room closed.

end_partial.architect: Six hundred. He never learned what you knew. Room closed.

end_dark.architect: Paid in full. Remembered in full. Room closed.

end_loss.architect: Three hundred and fifty. Room closed.

afterword.speaker: nabil_haddad
afterword.clean: Good tenant. Knew the law. I gave back. It's fine.
afterword.partial: Students. They take what you give.
afterword.dark: We need a lawyer, Karim. And tell everybody about this one.
